title: Trace Forensics: Weekly Sync + Cost Attribution Plan
decisions: Run a 2-week controlled sampling experiment across three customer cohorts (A/B/C) to validate trace sampling + prefix-KV attribution model.
Rename the existing 'trace-cost' dashboard to 'trace-attribution-lens' and add a view that maps spans->tokens->billing buckets.
Adopt hybrid sampling: session-level deterministic sampling + stochastic tail sampling for cold-path requests.
Temporarily hold off on lowering global sample rate until KV-cache mis-attribution is resolved (see hypothesis #2).
action_items: Maya: Draft the experiment runbook and success criteria; post to Confluence by 2026-11-14.
Ethan: Add 'span.flags' and 'kv-hit' labels to ingest pipeline; instrument ingestion to preserve token_count property (JIRA-OBS-1427) - due 2026-11-18.
Sofia: Prototype dashboard widgets showing cost-per-span and inferred token attribution; wire to sample data set - due 2026-11-19.
Liam: Create a lightweight patch for the runtime to emit KV-cache metadata in 90% of calls (opt-in flag) and bench overhead - PR by 2026-11-17.
Priya: Coordinate with billing to get token-price calibration for embeddings vs generation; capture edge-case SKUs - due 2026-11-20.
All: Join 2026-11-16 kickoff call to finalize cohort mapping and sampling seeds.
content:
Summary:

This week’s sync focused on the recurring problem where traced-span counts and the usage-based billing metrics diverge in high-KV-cache workloads. We sketched an experiment to better attribute ingestion and egress costs back to spans and ultimately to customer routes. The goal: reduce unexplained cost variance by 40% in two weeks and produce an operational dashboard that makes root causes discoverable in < 10 minutes.

Context / problem statement:
- Multiple incidents in Oct-Nov where cost spikes correlated with increased trace volume but billing didn't linearly follow; suspicion that cached prefixes and repeated KV-cache hits are mis-attributed or double-counted in telemetry.
- Current trace pipeline strips some runtime metadata to reduce payload size; we lack reliable mapping from span -> token_count -> model SKU.
- Dashboards show high-level token delta but we can't tell which spans are responsible for tail cost (rare long sequences) vs bulk cheap ops (embeddings).

Hypotheses:
1) Sampling bias: our tail-heavy sampling skews observed span distribution toward expensive traces, overstating per-request cost when extrapolated to full traffic.
2) KV-cache mis-attribution: when runtime serves from KV cache, telemetry loses the original request token_count and the cache-hit is recorded as a separate cheap span, breaking attribution.
3) SKU mapping gaps: embeddings vs generation pricing not reconciled in pipeline. Billing uses SKU tags but some runtime variants omit the SKU label.

Proposed experiment (high level):
- 3 cohorts (A: control, current sampling; B: session-deterministic 1% sample w/ full metadata; C: hybrid sampling: deterministic at session start + tail probabilistic).
- Duration: 14 days to capture weekday/weekend patterns and both PLG and enterprise traffic.
- Instrumentation additions: span.flags, kv_hit boolean, original_token_count (if available), model_sku label.
- Measurement: p50/p95/p99 per-span cost, ratio of observed token_count to billing token delta, unexplained cost fraction.
- Success criteria: unexplained cost fraction decreases by >= 40% for cohort B/C vs control; dashboards enable a 3-click drilldown to the top-3 root causes for >70% of observed spikes.

Dashboard / UX work:
- New dashboard: 'trace-attribution-lens' (rename and expand existing). Tabs: Panorama (aggregate token delta & cost), Root cause (top spans by inferred cost), KV-heatmap (routes x kv-hit rate), SKU-recon (model_sku mappings and suspected mismatches).
- Widget notes: need ability to toggle extrapolation method (naive scaling vs weighted by sessions).
- Will add a small 'investigate' template to auto-populate a new ticket with top spans + sample trace link.

Runtime changes (brief):
- Emit KV-cache metadata with opt-in flag to limit overhead during experiment. Liam will attach a microbench.
- Ensure runtime includes model_sku label in trace context for any upgraded model pipelines.

Risks & mitigations:
- Overhead from extra labels increases telemetry egress (cost/regret). Mitigation: run opt-in on small percentage first; monitor telemetry ingestion cost; revert if >5% ingestion uplift.
- Privacy concerns: we must not include raw prompt text. Only token_count and non-PHI flags are OK. Add a short privacy note to runbook.
- Attribution mismatch may persist if billing windows/aggregation differ; align with billing team on sampling extrapolation method (Priya).

Open questions / notes-to-self:
- If KV cache hides original token_count, can we reconstruct via sampled request snapshots? (priority: high)
- How to reconcile embeddings billed per-vector vs token-based traces — likely need a separate mapping table in telemetry.
- Consider moving high-cardinality labels into an attachable metadata blob rather than top-level labels to reduce cardinality explosion.

Experiment telemetry plan (practical):
- Create an internal topic 'trace-attrib-experiment' to capture full traces for cohorts B/C for the experiment window; retention 7d, limited to dev/staging and a small percent of prod traffic initially.
- Add a pipeline step that computes inferred_cost = token_count * sku_price and emits delta vs reported billing sample.

Meeting notes (time-stamped):
- 09:05 - Quick sync on incidents: Ana summarized that two incidents traced to a new runtime patch that changed KV metadata shape.
- 09:18 - Ethan walked through the drafting of JIRA-OBS-1427; main ask is preserving token_count at ingestion.
- 09:35 - Sofia demoed a prototype widget showing cost-per-span waterfall (ugly but useful). Feedback: need route grouping and exclude healthcheck noise.
- 09:50 - Decision checkpoint: cohort experiment approved, dashboards prioritized over full rollout.

Follow-ups for next sync (2026-11-19):
- Review runbook after Maya posts it; confirm cohort mapping and seeds.
- Ethan to provide an ingestion cost estimate for extra labels.
- Liam to present bench results for opt-in KV flag.
- Sofia to iterate on dashboard with route filter and sample-trace links.

Appendix (quick references):
- Minimal runbook checklist (to be expanded): 1) cohort config; 2) sampling seeds; 3) telemetry labels list; 4) retention & alerting thresholds; 5) rollback criteria.
- Useful queries (handy):
  - top spans by inferred_cost last_24h: SELECT span_name, SUM(inferred_cost) ...
  - kv_hit rate by route: SELECT route, AVG(kv_hit) ...
  - billing vs observed token delta: JOIN billing_samples ON window

Random brainstorming bullets (informal):
- Could we compress the model_sku label into a small enum to avoid cardinality? e.g., e1/g3/vector-small.
- Might be worth a 'trace-slab' microservice that performs expensive attribution offline and writes back summarized attributions.
- If experiment shows deterministic sampling works better for attribution, update global sampling policy but only after second validation window.

End notes:
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic; aim is to ship a small observable improvement quickly rather than a perfect attribution system. Expect iteration.

-- Maya
